setup_protocol: Coordinator captures self boot/UID/EUID/PID/PPID/birth and inherited product dev/inode/mode/owner/size/mtime/ctime baseline. Creates dedicated bounded private pipes, nonblocking ends, closes all unused ends in every role.

Fork controller first; controller publishes bounded identity+nonce ready packet, then parks on its sole coordinator-control pipe. Coordinator validates fresh fork PID/PPID/UID/EUID/boot/birth and opens controller pidfd before creating guard. No PID is accepted externally.

Coordinator forks guard carrying anchored controller pidfd/product/t0; guard closes controller-control writer and unrelated descriptors, publishes private guard identity+nonce and parks on sole coordinator start pipe. Coordinator binds own-fork guard PID/PPID/birth/boot/UID/EUID/product and acquires matching guard pidfd before sending GUARD_START. Only after validated GUARD_START may guard fork worker. Worker closes unrelated controller/report descriptors, publishes private ready identity+nonce and parks on sole guard control pipe.

Guard opens worker pidfd before release, binds owned fork PID/PPID/birth/boot/UID/EUID/nonce and rechecks inherited product identity and finite monotonic time. Guard must detect controller pidfd readability during every setup/progress wait. Controller loss before complete readiness is a negative setup failure, never controllerloss-success.

Guard forwards bounded readiness packet to coordinator only after worker identity/pidfd binding. Coordinator validates it; only then issues fixed case action. Packet sizes bounded below PIPE_BUF, exact length/magic/nonce/role checks; short reads use bounded accumulation rather than trusting partial packet.

Normal coordinator sends NORMAL_ARM only after complete guard+worker readiness. Guard validates worker-stop intent, identity/product/deadlines and controller still live, records normal armed before returning exact NORMAL_ARM_ACK. Coordinator validates ACK before sending controller orderly quit. Guard directs worker orderly completion, verifies worker exit using its pidfd and its own matching waitpid. Controller exit is expected only after NORMAL_ARM; coordinator independently pidfd-observes/reaps controller exit0.

Controllerloss coordinator sends LOSS_ARM only after complete guard+worker readiness. Guard revalidates identity/product/time/controller live and records loss armed before exact LOSS_ARM_ACK. Coordinator validates ACK then sends fixed deliberate controller exit command. Guard requires exact controller pidfd exit event plus unchanged own/worker identity/product/deadline before one symbolic SYS_pidfd_send_signal(workerfd,SIGKILL,NULL,0). No PID-kill fallback or signal retry; guard never reaps controller.

Guard observes exact worker pidfd exit and is the sole worker waitpid parent; returns bounded terminal facts packet before exit. Coordinator drains terminal report with finite deadline before reap; independently matches its controller and guard waitpid statuses. Parsed report success cannot replace actual syscall/poll/wait outcomes.
